body.heading: Where in the world is Sudan?
paragraphs: Sudan is a country in Northern Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Sudan is Khartoum.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Sudan speak Arabic and English.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Sudan is the Sudanese pound.

body.heading: How big is Sudan?
paragraphs: Sudan covers about 1,886,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about twice the size of Tanzania.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt! At Meroë, dozens of steep, slender pyramids built by the kings and queens of Kush rise from the desert sand.
In Khartoum you can stand where the Blue Nile and White Nile flow together to form the great Nile River, and take a boat past Tuti Island's farms.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Sudan on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Sudan in one breath: a country in Northern Africa, capital Khartoum, where people speak Arabic and pay with the Sudanese pound.
materials: A globe, atlas or world map (to find Sudan)
Paper and crayons or pencils for the screen-free mission
supervision: Read this one together: a grown-up can help with tricky place names and hunt for Sudan on the map as you read.
